Given, $E$ (in $eV$ ) $= \dfrac{12375}{\lambda ( inÅ )}$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\overset{→}{E} = {10}^{- 3}\cos \left[\dfrac{2\pix}{5 \times {10}^{- 7}} - 2\pi \times 6 \times {10}^{14}t\right]\overset{^}{x}N / c$
$k = \dfrac{2\pi}{5 \times {10}^{- 7}}$
And $\omega = 6 \times {10}^{14} \times 2\pi⇒ f = 6 \times {10}^{14}Hz$
$E = ϕ + K{E}_\max$

$∴$ Stopping potential is $0.48V$

questions.q:
A photo-emissive substance is illuminated with a radiation of wavelength $\lambda_i$ so that it releases electrons with de-Broglie wavelength $\lambda_e$. The longest wavelength of radiation that can emit photoelectron is $\lambda_0$. Expression for de-Broglie wavelength is given by :
( $\mathrm{m}:$ mass of the electron, $\mathrm{h}:$ Planck's constant and $c$ : speed of light)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{K}. \mathrm{E}=\mathrm{E}-\mathrm{W} \\ & \lambda_{\mathrm{e}}=\frac{\mathrm{h}}{\sqrt{2 \mathrm{mK} \cdot \mathrm{E}}}, \mathrm{E}=\frac{\mathrm{hc}}{\lambda_{\mathrm{i}}}, \mathrm{W}=\frac{\mathrm{hc}}{\lambda_0} \\ & \frac{\mathrm{~h}^2}{2 \mathrm{~m} \lambda_{\mathrm{e}}^2}=\frac{\mathrm{hc}}{\lambda_{\mathrm{i}}}-\frac{\mathrm{hc}}{\lambda_0} \\ & \lambda_{\mathrm{e}}=\sqrt{\frac{\mathrm{h}}{2 \mathrm{mc}\left(\frac{1}{\lambda_{\mathrm{i}}}-\frac{1}{\lambda_0}\right)}}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: Let ${K}_{1}$ and ${K}_{2}$ be the maximum kinetic energies of photo-electrons emitted when two monochromatic beams of wavelength ${λ}_{1}$ and ${λ}_{2}$, respectively are incident on a metallic surface. If ${λ}_{1} = 3{λ}_{2}$ then :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
According to Einstein's photoelectric equation

$\dfrac{h c}{λ} = {ϕ}_{0} + {KE}_\max$,~where ${ϕ}_{0}$~is a work function of a metal

$∴ {K }_{1} = \dfrac{h c}{{λ}_{1}} - {ϕ}_{0} \ldots \left(\text{i}\right)

${K }_{2} = $\dfrac{h c}{{λ}_{2}} - {ϕ}_{0} \ldots \left(\text{i} \text{i}\right)

\text{or}{K}_{1} - {K}_{2} =$hc \left[\dfrac{1}{\lambda1} - \dfrac{1}{\lambda2}\right]$

~ $= hc\left[\dfrac{1}{3\lambda2} - \dfrac{1}{\lambda2}\right] = - \dfrac{2hc}{3{λ}_{2}} \left(\text{Given}{λ}_{1} =3{λ}_{2}\right)$

~ $= - $\dfrac{2}{3} \left({K }_{2} + {ϕ}_{0}\right)\left(\text{Using (ii)}\right)$

$or {K }_{1} = {K }_{2} - $\dfrac{2}{3} {K }_{2} - \dfrac{2}{3} {ϕ}_{0} = \dfrac{{K }_{2}}{3} - \dfrac{2}{3} {ϕ}_{0}

$\text{or} {K }_{1}< \dfrac{{K }_{2}}{3}$

questions.q: The de Broglie wavelength of an electron having kinetic energy $E$~is $\lambda$. If the kinetic energy of electron becomes $\dfrac{E}{4}$, then its de-Broglie wavelength will be:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The de-Broglie wavelength in the first case is&

$\lambda = \dfrac{h}{2mE}$

In the second case the kinetic energy is~$K = \dfrac{E}{4}$.

Let the de-Broglie wavelength be~$\lambda '$.

The value of wavelength is

$\lambda ' = \dfrac{h}{2m\dfrac{E}{4}} = \dfrac{2h}{2mE} = 2\lambda$

questions.q:
Monochromatic light of frequency $6 \times {10}^{14}Hz$ is produced by a laser. The power emitted is $2 \times {10}^{- 3}W .$ How many photons per second on an average, are emitted by the source?

(Given $h = 6 . 63 \times {10}^{- 34}Js$)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Energy of a single photon is given by, $hν$. Therefore, power can be written as

$P = nhv$

$⇒ n = \dfrac{P}{hν} = \dfrac{2 \times {10}^{- 3}}{6 . 63 \times {10}^{- 34} \times 6 \times {10}^{14}}$

$= 5 \times {10}^{15}$

questions.q: An electron, a doubly ionized helium ion ($He^{++}$) and proton are having the same kinetic energy. The relation between their respective de-Broglie wavelength~$\lambdae^{*}\lambda{He}^{+ +}$ and~${λ}_{p}$ is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\lambda=\frac{h}{m v}=\frac{h}{\sqrt{2 m k}}$
$\lambda_{\mathrm{e}}: \lambda_{\mathrm{p}}: \lambda_{{He}^{++}}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{\mathrm{m}_{\mathrm{e}}}}: \frac{1}{\sqrt{\mathrm{m}_{\mathrm{p}}}}: \frac{1}{\sqrt{\mathrm{He}^{++}}}$
$\frac{1}{\sqrt{9.1 \times 10^{-31}}}: \frac{1}{\sqrt{1.6 \times 10^{-27}}}: \frac{1}{\sqrt{4 \times 1.6 \times 10^{-27}}}=84: 2: 1$

questions.q: If the two metals $A$ and $B$ are exposed to radiation of wavelength $350$ nm. The work functions of metals $A$ and $B$ are $4 . 8eV\text{and}2 . 2eV$. Then choose the correct option
options: Both metals $A$ and $B$ will emit photo-electrons
Both metals $A$ and $B$ will not emit photoelectrons
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
As we know, for photoelectric emission,& $hν > ϕ$.

Now,

$hν = \dfrac{hc}{λ} = \dfrac{1240}{350}eV = 3 . 54eV$

Therefore, only metal $B$ will emit photoelectrons.

questions.solution:
$hν = W + \dfrac{{V}_{0}}{2}e$

$⇒ {ν}_{0} = \dfrac{3}{2}ν$

questions.q: An electron (mass $m$ ) with initial velocity $\overset{→}{v} = {v}_{0}\overset{^}{i} + {v}_{0}\overset{^}{j}$ is in an electric filed $\overset{→}{E} = - {E}_{0}\overset{^}{k} .$ If ${\lambda}_{0}$ is initial de-Broglie wavelength of electron, its de-Broglie wave length at time $t$ is given by:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Initial velocity of electron,&

$v = {v}_{0}\overset{^}{i} + {v}_{0}\overset{^}{j} ⇒ \left|u\right| = \sqrt{{v}_{0}^{2} + {v}_{0}^{2}} = {v}_{0}\sqrt{2}$

Initial de Broglie wavelength associated with electron,~

${λ}_{0} = \dfrac{h}{p} = \dfrac{h}{m{v}_{0}\sqrt{2}}$

now,

$v = u + at$
Velocity as a function of time $= {v}_{0}\overset{^}{i} + {v}_{0}\overset{^}{j} + \dfrac{e{E}_{0}}{m}t\overset{^}{k}$
so wavelength $\lambda = \dfrac{h}{m\sqrt{2{v}_{0}^{2} + \dfrac{e^{2}{E}_{0}^{2}}{m^{2}}t^{2}}}$
$\lambda = \dfrac{{\lambda}_{0}}{\sqrt{1 + \dfrac{e^{2}{E}_{0}^{2}}{2m^{2}{v}_{0}^{2}}t^{2}}}$

questions.q:
In photoelectric effect
A. The photocurrent is proportional to the intensity of the incident radiation.
B. Maximum kinetic energy with which photoelectrons are emitted depends on the intensity of incident light.
C. Max& K.E. with which photoelectrons are emitted depends on the frequency of incident light.
D. The emission of photoelectrons require a minimum threshold intensity of incident radiation.
E. Max& K.E. of the photoelectrons is independent of the frequency of the incident light.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
With proper& energetic radiation, the photoelectric current increases with an increase in accelerating potential until it reaches a point where it reaches its maximum and does not increase with an additional increase in accelerating potential.

For a given potential difference, the photocurrent is directly proportional to the intensity of the incident radiation.

The maximum kinetic energy of the emitted photoelectrons can be written as

${K}_\max = hν - \phi$

From above equation, it can be seen that the maximum kinetic energy of the photoelectron& depends on the frequency of the light used.

Hence, the statements A and C are correct.

questions.q: A nucleus of mass $M$ at rest splits into two parts having masses $\dfrac{M '}{3}$ and $\dfrac{2M^{'}}{3}  \left(M^{'} < M\right). The ratio of de Broglie wavelength of two parts will be$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Since the initial momentum of the system is zero. To keep the final momentum zero, the momentum of both parts should be equal and opposite in direction.

\left|\overset{→}{P}1\right| = \left|\overset{→}{P}2\right|$

Here $\overset{→}{P}$ is momentum

De-Broglie wavelength is given by~$\lambda = \dfrac{h}{P}$

Hence, both will have same de Broglie wavelength.

Therefore,~${λ}_{1}: {λ}_{2} = 1: 1$.

$

questions.q:
The equation $\lambda = \dfrac{1 . 227}{x}nm$ can be used to find the de-Broglie wavelength of an electron. In this equation $x$ stands for :
Where,
$m =$ mass of electron
$P =$~momentum of electron
$K =$ Kinetic energy of electron
$V =$ Accelerating potential in volts for electron
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The de-Broglie's wavelength& is given by& $\lambda = \dfrac{h}{mv}$, where,~$h$~is Planck's constant and~$v$~is velocity.

Using relation between momentum and kinetic energy, we have~$\lambda = \dfrac{h}{2m\left(KE\right)}$

Here, kinetic energy of electron is stated as~$KE = qV$.

Then, we have~$\lambda = \dfrac{h}{2mqV}$

Putting the values of $m = 9 . 1 \times {10}^{- 31}kgandq = 1 . 62 \times {10}^{- 19}C$~of electron

We get,~$\lambda = \dfrac{1 . 22}{V}nm$.

So,~$x$~stand for~$\sqrt{V}$.

questions.q: $In a photoelectric experiment, the wavelength of the light incident on a metal is changed from $300 \mathrm{nm}$ to $400 \mathrm{nm}$. The decrease in the stopping potential is close to :  \left(\frac{\mathrm{hc}}{\mathrm{e}}=1240 \mathrm{nm}-\mathrm{V}\right)$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Let $\phi=$ work function of the metal, $\frac{\mathrm{hc}}{\lambda_{1}}=\phi+\mathrm{eV}_{1}\frac{\mathrm{hc}}{\lambda_{2}}=\phi+\mathrm{eV}_{2} \quad \ldots \ldots$ (ii) Sutracting (ii) from (i) we get $\mathrm{hc}\left(\frac{1}{\lambda_{1}}-\frac{1}{\lambda_{2}}\right)=\mathrm{e}\left(\mathrm{V}_{1}-\mathrm{V}_{2}\right)\Rightarrow V_{1}-V_{2}=\frac{h c}{e}\left(\frac{\lambda_{2}-\lambda_{1}}{\lambda_{1} \cdot \lambda_{2}}\right)\left[
\lambda_{1}=300 nm
\lambda_{2}=400 nm
\frac{hc}{e}=1240 nm-V
\right]=(1240 \mathrm{nm}-\mathrm{v})\left(\frac{100 \mathrm{nm}}{300 \mathrm{nm} \times 400 \mathrm{nm}}\right)=1,03 \mathrm{~V} \approx 1 \mathrm{~V}$
